name: Steam Controller (2026)
notes: Issue #56, from PadForge discussion #337. Valve's 2026 Steam Controller, the one SDL calls Triton (k_eControllerType_SteamControllerTriton, controller_list.h: 28DE:1302 wired, 0x1303 BLE, 0x1304 and 0x1305 the Proteus and Nereid dongles). SDL_hidapi_steam_triton.c binds it on any interface of a wired unit and names it 'Steam Controller'. Unlike the Deck and the 2015 controller, Triton presents ONE HID interface carrying everything by report id: 0x40 mouse and 0x41 keyboard (its lizard reports live in the same descriptor rather than on their own interfaces), 0x42 the 53-byte controller state SDL reads as ID_TRITON_CONTROLLER_STATE, 0x45 the 45-byte BLE state, 0x43 battery, 0x79 wireless status, the 0x80..0x89 haptic and rumble output reports, and a 63-byte command channel on feature reports 1 and 2. The descriptor is verbatim from OpenPuck's ReversePuckFirmware (ctrl_usb.cpp CTRL_HID_DESC), an emulation of this controller that a live Steam client already accepts, and every report id in it matches SDL's own ID_TRITON_* constants. The feature answers are grounded on two independent reads of real hardware that agree record for record: OpenPuck's identity.cpp ATTR83 (read with 'scmd 1302 --up 1 83') and CouchTurtle/sc2-research docs/FIRMWARE_PROTOCOL.md, which logs the same five tags in the same order off a live controller and matches Steam's own update JSON on two of the values. The firmware build timestamp shipped here is the newer of the two real builds (0x6A18D057, 2026-05-28) so Steam sees a current unit. Consumers drive report 0x42 through SubmitRawReport; Steam's haptic writes arrive on OutputReceived as output reports 0x80 and up.

reports.comment: ID_GET_ATTRIBUTES_VALUES. The 25-byte attribute blob verbatim from a real 28DE:1302 (OpenPuck ReversePuckFirmware/identity.cpp, read with 'scmd 1302 --up 1 83'). As (tag, u32-LE) records: 01 product 0x1302, 02 capabilities, 0A bootloader build 0x68D2F92E, 04 firmware build 0x6A18D057, 09 board revision 0x48. Steam validates these byte for byte - two wrong bytes and it re-asks forever - so none of them is invented, and all of them are firmware and model values shared across units rather than per-device ones.
ID_GET_STRING_ATTRIBUTE index 0, the board serial, in Valve's own format.
Index 1, the unit serial. Constant, as every serial this catalog ships is.
Index 3 is the one Steam actually checks: the Valve constant 7054257d2da7, the same on every real unit.

Any other index reads back 0xFF where the index would be, which is how a real unit says the string is not provisioned: Steam's own hardwareupdater tests that byte for 0xFF (CouchTurtle/sc2-research tools/attr_query.py, read out of the shipped updater bundle).
Wireless transport state. 0x01 = wired, no radio link up.

ID_SET_SETTINGS_VALUES reads back as the settings block the host just wrote. Verified on a real Steam Deck answering a real Steam client: five SET/GET pairs in that capture, every reply byte-identical to its write. Steam performs this read during the claim, and a device that stalls it never finishes being claimed. Triton's channel rides feature report 1, so the echo carries that report id back too.

layout.note: The controller interface is an opaque vendor blob addressed by report id, as the real device's is, so it declares no axes or buttons for a layout to reference. Report 0x42 carries the full shape. Same convention as the steam-controller and steam-deck-composite profiles.
